# Offset tests (E1, E3, R1; generated by stats.py)

delta = gap*(m) - gap*(2): how much faster (in log2 units of isolated learning time) the complex feature must be, relative to the linear control, before the network is indifferent. delta < 0 is a residual simplicity preference. Bootstrap: 2000 resamples of seeds (joint and isolated runs) within cells. SESOI = 0.5 log2 units (a 1.41x speed ratio). p_holm: Holm-adjusted within each (experiment, depth) family of four tests. 'pooled' = mean offset over both optimisers and m = 3, 5.

## Sample-size projection from these data (5 seeds per cell)

MDE = smallest offset detectable with 80% power at two-sided alpha = .05 with the current seeds. 'seeds for |delta| = x' = seeds per cell needed to detect an offset of size x, same grid. Normal approximation from the bootstrap SE; not observed power.
